Public Portion 
 1. Discussion of Proposed Woodland Ordinance Draft. 
 
Minutes: 
On September 24, 2026, the Sustainability & Environment Committee, chaired by Councilor 
Victor Davila, met to continue its review of the proposed Woodland Ordinance. The committee 
reviewed the latest draft with representatives from the Law Department, SCANS, and the City 
Forestry Division. The proposed ordinance is intended to address tree canopy loss associated 
with development while balancing impacts on homeowners and City operations. The draft 
generally applies to parcels of at least 5,000 square feet that meet additional tree or canopy 
requirements. 
 
The committee discussed parcel size, tree-removal thresholds, permit and mitigation fees, 
homeowner protections, enforcement, and the City's ability to administer the ordinance. City 
Forester Alex Sherman raised concerns about the staffing and resources needed for effective 
enforcement and previously recommended increasing the minimum parcel size to reduce the 
impact on individual homeowners. SCANS representatives discussed maintaining protections 
against significant tree canopy loss while avoiding unnecessary burdens on residents and 
development. The committee identified areas of the draft requiring additional clarification and 
review, including applicability, fee structure, and administrative procedures. 
No formal vote was taken. The committee scheduled a final review of the proposed ordinance for 
October 9, 2026, at 2:00 p.m., with the goal of presenting it to the full City Council on October 
19 for first-step consideration. The ordinance would then return to committee for further review 
before possible final consideration in November. The latest draft Woodland Ordinance was the
document reviewed.  
The meeting adjourned at 2:58 p.m.
